title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: THE LEAD, AND THE BIGGEST ITEM THIS REPORT HAS CARRIED — OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra on September 3, verified on OpenAI's own launch page rather than a tracker; it takes the computer-use crown outright (OSWorld 2.0 72.6% vs Opus 5's 70.2%, ScreenSpot-Pro 92.7%, Agents' Last Exam 59.3% vs Opus 5's 55.5% at ~65% fewer output tokens), leads Terminal-bench 4.0 at 57.9% over Fable 5.1's 55.8% AT ROUGHLY 9% LOWER COST PER TASK, prices at $10/$50 per MTok — identical to Fable 5.1 — and is the first model OpenAI has declared Critical for cybersecurity under its own Preparedness Framework
bullets.summary: Read directly off openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra, not off a ledger row: 'rolling out today to a limited set of organizations,' then ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise, the API as gpt-6-astra, and AWS Bedrock. $10 input / $50 output per MTok, fast mode at 2x speed for 2x price. Yesterday this report recorded Astra as 'forthcoming, not shipped'; that is now closed. Three things matter to a fleet whose primary work is an agent driving a computer. (a) COMPUTER USE: OSWorld 2.0 72.6% vs GPT-5.6 Sol's 65.7% in about 47% less wall-clock per task, ScreenSpot-Pro 92.7% vs Fable 5's 87.3%, Agents' Last Exam 59.3% against Claude Opus 5's 55.5% while spending ~65% fewer output tokens; with the updated Codex harness OpenAI claims 1.9x faster task completion on Mind2Web. (b) ALIGNMENT AS A MEASURED NUMBER, not a posture: on an internal computer-use safety benchmark (lower is better) Astra scores 2.4% against Sol's 22.0%, Fable 5.1's 9.5% and Opus 5's 11.5%; on an internal circumvention benchmark it never attempted to bypass a Codex auto-review denial even when auto-review was deliberately made evadable and the task was otherwise impossible; on a capability-hallucination benchmark 4.2% vs Sol's 12.2%. (c) CYBER: Astra meets the CRITICAL threshold under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework — ExploitBench 100% (Sol 78.5%), SRE-Bench 88.0% one-shot (Sol 55.9%), and during evaluation it discovered and used TWO PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN ZERO-DAYS, now disclosed to maintainers. The shipping version refuses advanced offensive tasks; looser safeguards come later via OpenAI Daybreak. One further item sits directly on this ecosystem's own tooling: Higgsfield's CEO is quoted in the launch post saying Astra executes their most complex creative workflows using up to 20% fewer tokens than other models tested. Also new: in Codex, Astra keeps NOTES ACROSS CONTEXT WINDOWS with earlier windows left searchable, instead of compacting them into a lossy summary — an experimental config.toml flag becoming the default in weeks.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the first frontier release in this corpus that changes a decision rather than a number. The Construct's actual workload IS computer use — Cowork driving the Mac, Claude-in-Chrome driving tabs, Hermes driving credentialed deploys — and that is precisely the axis Astra leads on, at the same $10/$50 Fable 5.1 charges. But note what does NOT follow: this fleet's harness, its ~130 skills, its gates and its whole operating model are Claude-native, and Terminal-bench 4.0 57.9% vs 55.8% is a two-point gap, not a reason to rebuild. The honest read is that the computer-use gap (OSWorld, ScreenSpot-Pro, Agents' Last Exam) is real and wider than the coding gap, so the cheap move is a bounded bake-off on ONE real job — a B9 answer-page deploy-and-verify, or a GSC/GA abrasion pull — measured on cost per completed task, which is exactly the discipline yesterday's bullet 2 established and which no benchmark board can run for us. Two items are worth reading beyond the routing question. First, the alignment numbers are the same behaviours this fleet encodes by hand in verify-before-claiming and review-build-before-claiming-done, now published as benchmarks with figures attached; that gives our gates a scoreboard they did not have. Second, the Codex notes-across-context-windows design is a direct answer to a failure this corpus has logged repeatedly — compaction silently dropping the record of completed work, which is the exact problem reconcile-before-building exists to work around. For Brand 9 and PRAGMA: no direct bearing, EXCEPT the Higgsfield quote, since Higgsfield is a live paid dependency in the B9/VironBox render path and its vendor is now publicly optimising against Astra.

bullets.title: Claude Code 2.1.260 (September 3) is a security release wearing a changelog's clothes — it fixes permission rules containing parentheses being SILENTLY DROPPED, which left folders marked read-only actually writable by the Bash sandbox; it fixes zsh command substitution smuggled through REPORTTIME/REPORTMEMORY/DIRSTACKSIZE being auto-approved; and it REVERTS the 2.1.259 change this report led with yesterday
bullets.summary: Date-verified by fetching code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog and reading the <Update label="2.1.260" description="September 3, 2026"> heading, with 2.1.259 (September 2) beneath it — so the Claude Code channel shipped on two consecutive days while the Platform channel stayed silent. Three fixes are security-grade and are stated as such in the vendor's own words. (1) Edit/Write/Read permission rules whose path contains parentheses were dropped as invalid or ignored by the Bash sandbox, 'which left "read-only" folders writable' — a deny rule that appeared to be in force and was not. (2) A single file permission rule with an uncompilable pattern (e.g. an unclosed '[') made EVERY file edit fail with 'Invalid regular expression'; such a deny rule now guards the literal path it spells. (3) Bash permission checks were auto-approving zsh commands that hid a command substitution inside a REPORTTIME, REPORTMEMORY or DIRSTACKSIZE assignment; these now prompt. Beyond permissions: blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories on macOS was hiding the user's git config from sandboxed git and hiding a worktree-isolated subagent's own checkout; managed settings were not loading for claude.ai Enterprise/Team users who still had a leftover API key from an earlier /login, and /status listed a signed-in account and a configured API key as if both were in effect. And the item with direct continuity: 2.1.260 REVERTS the 2.1.259 change that applied Read() deny rules to Bash arguments, because it denied 'npm run build' under a Read(./**/build/**) rule in every mode. Yesterday this report led with 2.1.259; part of that release did not survive twenty-four hours. Also fixed, and specific to this environment: the Artifact tool's first call failing with an 'Invalid tool parameters' validation error in some Cowork sessions; Claude in Chrome tools failing with 'Not connected' mid-task when a connector was added or removed; a subagent resumed via SendMessage never being woken by that agent's completion; agent-team transcripts losing messages during long API retry waits; and intermittent 'task output swap refused' errors when many sessions share a project directory. New features: a /diff panel beside the conversation in fullscreen, a likely-cause explanation for prompt-cache misses in /cost, and a text form of /advisor for headless (-p/Agent SDK) and Remote Control sessions.
bullets.how: YES, and the parentheses bug converts a four-day-old standing limit into an urgent one. This report has now recorded for a FIFTH consecutive day that claude --version has not been read on the fleet. Until yesterday that was a tidiness problem. Today it is a security question with a concrete shape: any machine here running below 2.1.260 with a permission rule whose path contains a parenthesis has a deny rule that looks enforced and is not, and this fleet's paths are full of parentheses — recovered folders, dated backups, macOS 'Application Support' trees, the _RECOVERED_2026-06-24 directory this very file is written into. Three actions, cheapest first. (a) Run claude --version on the Mac and on any box driving Hermes; it is one command and it has now been the prerequisite to five consecutive bullets. (b) Grep the settings files for permission rules containing '(' or '[' — the second bug means a single malformed rule can break every edit, and the first means a malformed rule can silently permit. (c) The 2.1.259 revert is its own lesson and belongs in the praxis log: yesterday's lead item shipped a rule that was withdrawn the next day, which argues for a one-release lag before adopting any permission-semantics change on machines that run unattended jobs. The Cowork Artifact-tool fix and the Chrome 'Not connected' fix both land on paths this ecosystem uses daily and are further argument for actually upgrading. No bearing on Brand 9 or PRAGMA.

bullets.title: SUPPLIER RISK, not product news — Anthropic will publish its IPO prospectus after Labor Day, hold an investor day in mid-September and could list as soon as late September or early October, at a reported $1.5–2T target against the $965B May Series H-1 mark, in what would be the largest IPO on record
bullets.summary: Reported September 3 across financial press. The S-1 was confidentially submitted to the SEC on June 1, 2026; the prospectus goes public after the holiday, with an investor day mid-September and a US listing targeted for late September or early October. Reported raise: more than $60B. Reported financials behind it: roughly $10.9B of revenue in Q2 2026 against $4.8B in Q1, a first operating profit of about $559M, and an annual run rate above $65B at the end of July. Anthropic has not set a share price, share count or listing date, and has said timing depends on market conditions — so every figure above is reporting and target, not a filed number. That distinction matters here because the prospectus itself, once public, becomes the first PRIMARY source this report will ever have had on the vendor underneath the entire Construct stack. Two dated items from yesterday's ledger sit inside the same window and are not coincidence: Anthropic's Claude Code weekly-limit reduction lands September 14, and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards are promised 'this fall' but not shipped.
bullets.how: MAYBE — nothing to do today, and one thing to put on the calendar. This ecosystem is single-vendor by construction: Cowork, Claude Code, the skills, the gates, the scheduled jobs and this report all sit on one supplier, and that supplier is about to become a public company with quarterly earnings, public guidance and shareholder pressure on gross margin. The near-term signal is already dated — the September 14 weekly-limit reduction is exactly the kind of unit-economics move a company tightens ahead of a listing, and it lands ten days from now on the plans this fleet actually runs on. The concrete action is small: when the prospectus publishes, read the risk factors and the revenue-concentration disclosure, because it is the only document that will ever say plainly what proportion of Anthropic's revenue comes from API versus subscription and how the consumer plans are priced against cost. That is a better input to any 'should we diversify the harness' question than a benchmark table — and read against bullet 1, the diversification question is now on the table for the first time in this corpus's history. No bearing on Brand 9 or PRAGMA.

bullets.title: METHOD — the week's 'efficiency claims invert under measurement' pattern BROKE today, and it broke on a release the preferred vendor-dated ledger could not have carried: the ledger's own as-of stamp (September 3) is a CEILING on what it can know, so a same-day frontier launch is only visible from the vendor primary
bullets.summary: Two findings, both corrections to how this report was reading its sources. FIRST, the pattern established over the last 48 hours — Gemini 3.8 Flash's cost per task up ~40% and Muse Spark 1.3's up from $0.40 to $0.55, both while advertising efficiency — does not hold for Astra. OpenAI publishes estimated cost-per-task COMPARISONS alongside the wins rather than instead of them: Terminal-bench 4.0 57.9% at ~9% lower estimated API cost than Fable 5.1 and ~63% lower than the Gemini configuration shown; Terminal-Bench Science 64.6% at ~31% lower cost than Fable 5.1; BenchCAD 95.9% at ~86% lower cost than Fable 5.1; GPQA Diamond exceeding Sol's best at ~37% lower cost. Those are still VENDOR-RUN figures and belong in the same sceptical bucket as Meta's, but the shape is different: a claim stated in the currency the buyer pays in, with the comparison model named. Yesterday's rule stands and gains a corollary — per-token price is not cost, AND a vendor that publishes cost per task against a named competitor has made a falsifiable claim, which is strictly more useful than one that publishes token counts. SECOND, and the more transferable half: the ledger this report chose YESTERDAY as its preferred source, precisely because it publishes its dating rule, does not carry Astra. It is not wrong — its methodology section states 'Collected September 3, 2026' and its FAQ answers 'as of September 3' with six rows and no OpenAI. The as-of timestamp did its job and disclosed the boundary honestly. The failure mode would have been ours: treating a well-methodologised ledger as complete rather than as complete-up-to-its-own-stamp.
bullets.how: YES, as method, and it closes a loop this corpus opened three days ago. The chain is now: fetch the page, read the dated heading, read the neighbouring entries, prefer a source that separates vendor date from listing date — and, new today, READ THE SOURCE'S AS-OF STAMP AS A CEILING AND GO TO THE VENDOR PRIMARY FOR ANYTHING DATED INSIDE THE LAST 24 HOURS. A curated source is always at least one collection-cycle behind the thing it curates, and the better the curation the more convincing its silence looks. That transfers verbatim to every feed a Construct agent treats as ground truth: brand-insights/latest.json, the flywheel registries, this file's own latest.json, each of which carries a 'generated' timestamp for exactly this reason and each of which will look authoritative while being stale. On the cost half: when this fleet runs the Astra bake-off proposed in bullet 1, the number to record is cost per completed job on our own work, because that is the only figure no vendor gets to publish.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP, each null established by fetching the page and naming the heading read — Anthropic PLATFORM silent for a THIRD consecutive day while Claude Code shipped twice, no MCP server or spec release, no arXiv paper dated in window, no material agent round (two small seeds only), and the signage / wayfinding / permitting MCP negative holds a FIFTEENTH day
bullets.summary: ANTHROPIC PLATFORM: release-notes overview fetched this fire; newest heading is still '### September 1, 2026' (Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, cache reads $0.25/MTok, tool_choice any/tool returning 400, per-message effort beta), with August 27 beneath it. No September 2, 3 or 4 entry — so the two first-party Anthropic channels have now diverged for a third straight day, Claude Code shipping 2.1.259 AND 2.1.260 while Platform published nothing. COWORK / SKILLS / PLUGINS: nothing dated in the window; the newest items remain the mid-August Chrome side-panel integration and the plugin marketplace launch. MCP: no server and no spec release; newest items are still the 2026-07-28 stateless specification and the August 22 roadmap update — a SIXTH consecutive week with no protocol movement, which is now a fact about the protocol's cadence rather than a gap in the searching. ARXIV: agent-architecture and context-engineering searches returned only papers outside the window (2603.09619, 2510.04618, 2602.05447, 2606.20683, 2507.13334, 2602.14690, 2602.20478), so logged null rather than padded with a stale citation. AGENT FUNDING: no material round dated in window. Two small seeds are dated September 3 and are recorded without bullets — Zeit AI (Munich, autonomous data-engine, EUR 5M seed, Y Combinator / Oxford Seed Fund / Sequoia Scout) and Souk (London, an agent named Coco for dormant-partnership reactivation, $1.6M pre-seed led by Sure Valley Ventures). Neither is an agent-platform round; both are verticalised applications, which is itself the shape of the current seed market. SIGNAGE: a fifteenth consecutive check returned only digital-signage CMS connectors (NoviSign via an integration platform), sign-company marketing pages, and a signage-lifecycle SaaS (SignAgent) that is a hosted product, not an MCP layer.
bullets.how: NO on the market items. The signage negative carries its standing clarification unchanged: the digital-signage CMS vendors that keep surfacing are screen and content-management tools, a different trade from the physical sign fabrication, monument and permitting work Brand 9 actually does, and the negative is about the latter and remains total. Fifteen consecutive checks is a settled fact about the market — the permitting and wayfinding-spec layer for the physical trade has no incumbent to displace. This report continues to record the open window rather than recommend building into it. One null is worth reading as signal rather than absence: the Platform channel's third silent day alongside two Claude Code releases means the harness is now moving materially faster than the API underneath it, which is where a fleet built on skills and gates rather than on raw API calls actually feels change.

praxis_lesson: A curated source is never more current than its own as-of stamp, and the better its methodology the more convincing its silence looks. Yesterday this report chose a ledger precisely because it publishes its dating rule — and today that ledger, correctly and honestly stamped 'collected September 3', simply does not contain the largest release of the week. It was not wrong; relying on it for a same-day launch would have been. So the rule extends one last time: fetch the page, read the dated heading, read the neighbours, prefer the source that separates vendor date from listing date, and then READ THE AS-OF STAMP AS A CEILING and go to the vendor's own primary for anything inside the last twenty-four hours. The corollary runs inward: every registry this ecosystem trusts — brand-insights/latest.json, the flywheel feeds, this file — carries a 'generated' field for the same reason, and each will look authoritative while being stale. The second lesson is cheaper and sharper. Claude Code 2.1.260 reveals that a permission rule containing a parenthesis was silently dropped, leaving folders marked read-only actually writable — and this report has now recorded for a FIFTH consecutive day that claude --version has not been read on the fleet. A limit carried long enough stops being a caveat and becomes the finding.
